gloss: to become ingrained; to soak in; to become a habit

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {染|し}み{付|つ}きませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {染|し}み{付|つ}いていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {染|し}み{付|つ}いていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to become ingrained; to soak into; to permeate
definitions.explanation: For a stain, smell, or habit to become deeply embedded and difficult to remove. Used both literally for physical substances and figuratively for habits, memories, and ways of thinking.

examples.japanese: {油|あぶら}の{匂|にお}いが{染|し}み{付|つ}いた。
examples.english: The smell of oil soaked in.

examples.japanese: タバコの{匂|にお}いが{服|ふく}に{染|し}み{付|つ}いた。
examples.english: The smell of cigarettes has permeated my clothes.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{習慣|しゅうかん}が{体|からだ}に{染|し}み{付|つ}いている。
examples.english: Years of habit have become ingrained in my body.

examples.japanese: {幼|おさな}い{頃|ころ}の{記憶|きおく}が{心|こころ}に{染|し}み{付|つ}いている。
examples.english: Childhood memories are deeply ingrained in my heart.

examples.japanese: {何年|なんねん}も{料理|りょうり}をしてきたので、{台所|だいどころ}に{油|あぶら}の{匂|にお}いが{染|し}み{付|つ}いて{取|と}れない。
examples.english: After years of cooking, the smell of oil has soaked into the kitchen and won't come out.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB STRUCTURE: {染|し}みる (to soak in/permeate) + {付|つ}く (to stick/attach)

TRANSITIVITY: Intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}).

CONJUGATION: Godan verb (-く type)
・{染|し}み{付|つ}かない (negative)
・{染|し}み{付|つ}きます (polite)
・{染|し}み{付|つ}いて (te-form)
・{染|し}み{付|つ}いた (past)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{匂|にお}いが{染|し}み{付|つ}く - smell permeates
・{習慣|しゅうかん}が{染|し}み{付|つ}く - habit becomes ingrained
・{体|からだ}に{染|し}み{付|つ}く - to become second nature
・{記憶|きおく}が{染|し}み{付|つ}く - memory becomes deeply embedded

NUANCE:
Implies something that has become so deeply embedded that it's difficult or impossible to remove or change. Often suggests a permanent or long-lasting state.

KANJI NOTE:
Also written as {染|し}みつく or しみつく.

REGISTER:
Neutral. Common in both spoken and written Japanese.
